marketing.description: homepage, feature, download, brand, and pricing-page marketing modules
instructions: Rewrite in the style of a native consumer-technology website for the target market. Sentence order, headline length, and calls to action may change, but product facts may not.
Keep the complete source meaning: do not add, remove, weaken, broaden, narrow, or substitute features, audiences, guarantees, comparisons, conditions, or claims.
Keep headings short, specific, and easy to scan. Lead with a user capability or outcome instead of an abstract corporate slogan.
Use a natural, explicit product-site call to action for the target language.

ui.description: navigation, buttons, forms, empty states, notifications, and settings
instructions: Keep copy short, consistent, and actionable. Use one term consistently for the same action.
Do not trade clarity for literary style or replace familiar UI labels with full sentences.

support.description: FAQ, help-center, illustrated tutorial, and troubleshooting modules
instructions: Use clear, reassuring, and actionable support-documentation language. Preserve the original order of steps.
Preserve all warnings concerning account deletion, subscriptions, backups, permissions, and device settings exactly.

technical.description: SDK, API, integration, and code-related documentation
instructions: Technical accuracy and terminology consistency take priority over marketing polish. Never translate code, identifiers, file names, paths, commands, parameters, or URLs.
Localize prose only when its technical meaning is fully preserved.

legal.description: privacy, refund, terms-of-service, settlement, and compliance content
instructions: Communicate the source strictly. Do not creatively rewrite, summarize, or add legal commitments.
This is draft-only content and requires human/legal review. It must not be published automatically.
